# Pinot Country — every record, flattened

## Chardonnay (variety)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/variety/chardonnay/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/variety/chardonnay.json
id: chardonnay
facets: colour=white · country=France
region: Burgundy, The world
what: Pinot's child by Gouais blanc, and the white grape sharing almost every hill in this directory. Where pinot goes, it follows — Burgundy, Champagne, the Willamette, Bien Nacido, Central Otago.
story: DNA work in the 1990s put the cross beyond argument: a pinot crossed with Gouais blanc produced chardonnay, aligoté, auxerrois, gamay, melon and eleven others. The Pinot parent need not have been pinot noir — any member of the family could have done it.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): Its parent, and the vine planted on the next row.
- kin → cote-de-beaune (region): Where the family split the hill: whites on one flank, reds on the other.
sources: s:wp-chardonnay — Chardonnay; s:wp-pinot-noir — Pinot noir
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Frühburgunder (variety)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/variety/fruhburgunder/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/variety/fruhburgunder.json
id: fruhburgunder
aliases: Pinot noir précoce · Early Burgundy · Blauer Frühburgunder
root: German früh (early) + Burgunder (Burgundian)
facets: colour=black · country=Germany
region: Ahr, Germany
what: An early-ripening pinot that comes in two to three weeks ahead of the rest. Germany kept it alive in the Ahr and on the Nahe when growers elsewhere pulled it out for cropping too lightly.
how: Small bunches, small berries, low yield, and a harvest date that beats autumn rain — useful where the season runs short.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The same family, running four to six weeks ahead of the latest clones.
- kin → ahr (region): The slate valley that kept it planted.
sources: s:wp-fr-hburgunder — Pinot Noir Précoce; s:wp-pinot-noir — Pinot noir
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Gamay (variety)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/variety/gamay/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/variety/gamay.json
id: gamay
aliases: Gamay noir à jus blanc
facets: colour=black · country=France
region: Burgundy
what: Pinot's other well-known child, banished from the Côte d'Or by ducal edict and sent south to granite, where it built Beaujolais.
story: *Tradition holds —* Philippe le Hardi ordered gamay out of the good slopes in 1395 and pinot noir back in. Whatever the duke's reasons, the split held: pinot took the limestone, gamay took the granite south of Mâcon.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): Same parentage story, opposite fate on the same hill.
- kin → burgundy (region): The region that expelled it from the Côte d'Or and still grows it further south.
sources: s:wp-gamay — Gamay; s:wp-pinot-noir — Pinot noir
provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-16

## Pinot blanc (variety)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/variety/pinot-blanc/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/variety/pinot-blanc.json
id: pinot-blanc
aliases: Weissburgunder · Pinot bianco · Klevner
facets: colour=white · country=France
region: Alsace
what: The white end of the family. A further mutation that can come from pinot gris or pinot noir and can go back the other way, which is why nurserymen watch their mother vines.
story: Henri Gouges found a white-berried shoot in his Nuits-Saint-Georges vineyard and propagated it; the wine is sold as Nuits-Saint-Georges blanc. *Inference —* nothing published suggests it is more than a selected mutation of the pinot noir already growing there.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The parent form; the mutation runs both ways.
- kin → pinot-gris (variety): Its neighbour on the colour ladder.
sources: s:wp-pinot-blanc — Pinot blanc; s:wp-pinot-noir — Pinot noir
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Pinot gris (variety)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/variety/pinot-gris/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/variety/pinot-gris.json
id: pinot-gris
aliases: Pinot Grigio · Grauburgunder · Ruländer
facets: colour=grey · country=France
region: Alsace
what: A colour sport of pinot: the berry loses most of its pigment and lands somewhere between grey, pink and bronze. Same vine, same bunch, different skin.
story: A somatic mutation in the VvMYBA1 or VvMYBA2 genes — the switches that tell a grape to make colour. It can arise from pinot noir or from pinot blanc, and it can revert.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The black form, and the one this site is about.
- kin → pinot-blanc (variety): The next mutation along the same path, in either direction.
- kin → alsace (region): Where it grows beside its black parent under the same appellation.
sources: s:wp-pinot-gris — Pinot gris; s:wp-pinot-noir — Pinot noir
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Pinot Meunier (variety)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/variety/pinot-meunier/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/variety/pinot-meunier.json
id: pinot-meunier
aliases: Meunier · Schwarzriesling · Müllerrebe
root: French meunier, miller — from the floury white hairs on the leaves
facets: colour=black · country=France
region: Champagne
what: Pinot noir with white down on its shoot tips and leaves — meunier means miller, and the vine looks dusted with flour. It buds later, ripens earlier and survives a frosty Champagne spring that kills its parent.
how: Genetically it is a chimera: two tissue layers, each carrying its own mutation, neither identical to pinot noir. Propagate it from the wrong layer and you get something else.
today: Champagne plants it heavily in the frost-prone Marne valley, and a handful of growers now bottle it alone.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The vine it mutated from, and cannot be a parent of.
- kin → champagne (region): Where it earns its keep: the valley floors that frost.
- kin → vendange-entiere (term): A press-house decision that treats it the same as its parent.
sources: s:wp-pinot-meunier — Pinot Meunier; s:wp-pinot-noir — Pinot noir
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Pinot noir (variety)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/variety/pinot-noir/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/variety/pinot-noir.json
id: pinot-noir
aliases: Pinot Noir · Spätburgunder · Blauburgunder · Pinot nero · Blauer Burgunder
said: PEE-noh NWAHR
root: French pin (pine) + noir (black) — the bunch is shaped like a pinecone · the cluster is small and conico-cylindrical
facets: colour=black · country=France
region: The world
what: A black grape from north-eastern France that ripens early, carries thin skin over tight pinecone-shaped bunches, and mutates more readily than almost any vine in cultivation. It gives pale wine with low tannin and high acid, and it rewards cold ground, which is why growers chase it toward the poles, the fog and the hills.
story: Pinot sits one or two generations from wild Vitis sylvestris, which makes it about as old as cultivated vines get. Crossed with the peasants' workhorse Gouais blanc somewhere in medieval north-eastern France, it fathered chardonnay, gamay, aligoté, auxerrois, melon and eleven more — half the vineyards of France descend from that one mismatch between the nobility's plot and the commoner's. *Tradition holds —* the dukes of Burgundy did the rest of the marketing.
how: Thin skins and little phenolic material give pale, medium-bodied, low-tannin wine. The same skins split and rot in a wet September. It buds early into frost, ripens early into heat, and its tight bunches trap moisture — every fault it has comes from the same anatomy that makes the wine taste the way it does.
today: Grown on every continent that can chill it: Burgundy and Champagne, Germany's Ahr and Baden, Oregon, California's fog corridors, Central Otago, Tasmania, Patagonia, the Cape.
- kin → burgundy (region): Home ground, and the reference every other pinot region gets measured against.
- kin → pinot-meunier (variety): A chimera of this vine — hairy leaves, earlier ripening, and a third of Champagne.
- kin → pinot-gris (variety): The same vine with the colour genes switched off partway.
- kin → chardonnay (variety): Its child, by Gouais blanc; the two share the same hillsides and the same cellars.
- kin → thin-skin (story): Every difficulty this grape hands a grower, in one place.
- kin → dijon-115 (clone): One of the numbered selections that let a grower buy this vine by catalogue.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/pinot-noir/pinot-noir-ov-pinot-noir.jpg · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Olivier Vanpé · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AOV-pinot-noir.jpg
sources: s:wp-pinot-noir — Pinot noir; s:wine-grapes-2012 — Wine Grapes: A Complete Guide to 1,368 Vine Varieties; s:oxford-companion-wine-4 — The Oxford Companion to Wine
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Ahr (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/ahr/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/ahr.json
id: ahr
facets: country=Germany · level=region · soil=slate, basalt, greywacke
region: Ahr, Germany
what: A narrow slate valley south of Bonn, among the smallest German regions and the one that gives more of its ground to spätburgunder than any other.
story: Steep terraces on a river that runs east-west, this far north, on dark stone that holds the day's heat. The July 2021 flood tore through the valley and its cellars; growers were still rebuilding years after.
geo: 50.54, 7.05 (region)
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): Called spätburgunder here, and grown in a higher share than anywhere else in Germany.
- kin → fruhburgunder (variety): The early-ripening cousin the valley kept.
- kin → baden (region): The other German pinot region, warmer and far larger.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/ahr/ahr-vineyard-in-the-ahr-valley-germany.jpg · CC0 1.0 · 1998alexkane · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AVineyard_in_the_Ahr_Valley%2C_Germany.jpg
sources: s:wp-ahr-wine-region — Ahr (wine region); s:wp-german-wine — German wine
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Alsace (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/alsace/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/alsace.json
id: alsace
facets: country=France · level=region
region: Alsace
what: A dry strip in the rain shadow of the Vosges where nearly everything is white — except pinot noir, the one red grape the appellation allows.
today: What used to be pale and often rosé now gets destemmed, barrel-aged and sold as red, and the 2022 rules brought thirteen grand cru sites into play for it. *Tradition holds —* the older bottles were lighter because nobody expected otherwise.
geo: 48.2, 7.35 (region)
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The only red the appellation permits.
- kin → pinot-gris (variety): Its grey sibling, grown on the same slopes.
- kin → baden (region): Across the Rhine, the same climate under another flag.
sources: s:wp-alsace-wine — Alsace wine
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-16

## Alto Adige (region)

id: alto-adige
aliases: Südtirol · South Tyrol
facets: country=Italy · level=doc
region: Alto Adige
what: German-speaking Italy, on terraces above Bolzano. Blauburgunder here is pinot nero on the label and Blauburgunder in the village, and it climbs as high as the frost allows.
geo: 46.5, 11.35 (region)
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): Called pinot nero and blauburgunder in the same village.
- kin → baden (region): The other Alpine pinot, north of the ridge.
sources: s:wp-south-tyrol-wine — South Tyrol wine

## Anderson Valley (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/anderson-valley/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/anderson-valley.json
id: anderson-valley
facets: country=United States · level=ava · established=1983
region: Anderson Valley, California
what: Mendocino's fog gap: a narrow valley along the Navarro River, open to the ocean at one end, redwoods at both edges. Sparkling houses came for the acid and stayed for the pinot.
story: The 1983 petition counted 47 acres of pinot noir. By 2025 the AVA farmed about 2,457 acres across roughly 100 vineyards, and the wineries buying from them mostly sit outside the valley.
geo: 39.0, -123.4 (region)
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The variety that took the valley over.
- kin → russian-river-valley (region): The other California fog corridor, an hour south.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/anderson-valley/anderson-valley-anderson-valley-pinot-noir-with-vineyard-in-background.jpg · CC BY 2.0 · Ethan Prater · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AAnderson_Valley_Pinot_noir_with_vineyard_in_background.jpg

## Baden (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/baden/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/baden.json
id: baden
facets: country=Germany · level=region · soil=loess, limestone, volcanic
region: Baden, Germany
what: Germany's warmest vineyards, in the Rhine rift between the Black Forest and the Vosges, facing Alsace across the river. Pinot in its three colours covers most of it.
how: Spätburgunder alone took 36.8% of Baden's vineyards in 2008 — 5,855 hectares — with grauburgunder and weissburgunder adding another fifth. The Kaiserstuhl, an old volcano on the valley floor, ripens the fullest of it.
geo: 48.1, 7.85 (region)
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): Spätburgunder: more than a third of the region's vines.
- kin → alsace (region): Same rift valley, other bank, similar size.
- kin → pinot-gris (variety): Grauburgunder, the second Burgundian here.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/baden/baden-bickensohl-kaiserstuhl-totenkopf-2004.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Jacquesverlaeken · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ABickensohl_Kaiserstuhl_Totenkopf_2004.jpg
sources: s:wp-baden-wine-region — Baden (wine region); s:wp-german-wine — German wine
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Burgundy (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/burgundy/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/burgundy.json
id: burgundy
aliases: Bourgogne
facets: country=France · level=region · established=1936 · soil=limestone and marl
region: Burgundy
what: A strip of limestone running south-west from Dijon where pinot noir and chardonnay have been sorted, fenced and argued over for a thousand years. Everything here is small: the hill is 40 km long and rarely 2 km wide, and it carries 100 appellations stacked in four ranks.
story: Medieval monks and the Valois dukes did the surveying: which parcel ripened, which drained, which froze. Denis Morelot wrote it down in 1831; Jules Lavalle classified it in 1855; the Beaune agricultural committee formalised it in 1861; and when the AOC laws arrived in 1936 most of Lavalle's first class became grands crus. The ranks on today's label are a nineteenth-century map given the force of law.
how: Four ranks, and the smaller the ground the louder the name. Grand cru takes 2% of production at 35 hl/ha and labels the vineyard alone. Premier cru takes 12% at 45 hl/ha and labels village plus vineyard. Village wines take 36% at 50 hl/ha across 42 villages. Regional Bourgogne carries the rest. A grower may always sell down a rank, never up.
today: UNESCO inscribed the climats in 2015, which put a heritage listing on a land-holding pattern rather than a building.
geo: 47.05, 4.85 (region)
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The grape this hill selected, and the one it exported.
- kin → cote-de-nuits (region): The northern half, holding nearly every red grand cru.
- kin → cote-de-beaune (region): The southern half, where the whites take the hill.
- kin → climat (term): The word for a named parcel, and the unit the whole system counts in.
- kin → hospices-de-beaune (org): The charity whose November auction sets the tone for the vintage.
- kin → how-pinot-travelled (story): How cuttings and arguments from this hill reached Oregon, Otago and the Cape.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/burgundy/burgundy-landscape-and-vineyards-in-bourgogne.jpg · CC BY-SA 2.0 · tara hunt · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ALandscape_and_vineyards_in_Bourgogne.jpg
sources: s:wp-burgundy-wine — Burgundy wine; s:unesco-1425 — The Climats, terroirs of Burgundy — World Heritage List 1425; s:wp-pinot-noir — Pinot noir; s:morris-inside-burgundy — Inside Burgundy: The Vineyards, the Wine and the People
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Casablanca Valley (region)

id: casablanca-valley
facets: country=Chile · level=doc
region: Casablanca Valley, Chile
what: Between Santiago and the port at Valparaíso, close enough to the Humboldt current for morning fog. Chile planted it in the 1980s to grow something other than cabernet.

- kin → pinot-noir (variety): Grown on the cool coastal side of the range.
- kin → anderson-valley (region): The same trick with fog, a hemisphere away.

## Central Otago (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/central-otago/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/central-otago.json
id: central-otago
facets: country=New Zealand · level=gi · soil=schist, loess, glacial gravel
region: Central Otago, New Zealand
what: The southernmost commercial wine region on earth, and the only part of New Zealand with a true continental climate — frost in the spring, forty-degree swings in a day, schist under everything.
story: Vines went from 92 hectares to 1,930 in about two decades. Pinot noir takes over 80% of the plantings, which is a bet no other region of this size has made.
geo: -45.02, 169.2 (region)
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): More than four fifths of everything planted here.
- kin → felton-road (producer): Bannockburn, and the cellar that made the region legible abroad.
- kin → rippon (producer): Lake Wanaka, and one of the most photographed vineyards anywhere.
- kin → abel-clone (clone): The cutting that walked through customs and changed New Zealand pinot.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/central-otago/central-otago-bannockburn-1-central-otago.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · AnnWoolliams · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ABannockburn_%281%29%2C_Central_Otago.jpg
sources: s:wp-central-otago-wine-region — Central Otago wine region; s:wp-new-zealand-wine — New Zealand wine
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Champagne (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/champagne/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/champagne.json
id: champagne
facets: country=France · level=region · soil=chalk
region: Champagne
what: Chalk country 150 km north-east of Paris where pinot noir is pressed off its skins within hours and comes out white. More pinot noir grows here than anywhere else in France, and almost none of it is red.
how: Five districts: Montagne de Reims, Vallée de la Marne, Côte des Blancs, Côte de Sézanne, the Aube. Pinot noir leads the Aube and does well on the Montagne; meunier holds the frost-prone Marne floors.
today: Coteaux Champenois lets a grower bottle the red instead, which in a warm year is no longer a curiosity.
geo: 49.05, 4.0 (region)
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): Grown for structure, not colour.
- kin → pinot-meunier (variety): Its frost insurance on the valley floor.
- kin → saignee (practice): The bleed that makes rosé, and the other way to use a black grape here.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/champagne/champagne-verzenay-vignoble.jpg · Public domain · Vassil · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AVerzenay_vignoble.jpg
sources: s:wp-champagne-wine-region — Champagne wine region; s:wp-champagne — Champagne
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

id: cote-chalonnaise
facets: country=France · level=district
region: Côte Chalonnaise, Burgundy
what: The same limestone, ten miles further south, at a third of the price. Bouzeron, Rully, Mercurey, Givry and Montagny — Mercurey and Givry do the red work.
geo: 46.75, 4.72 (region)
- kin → burgundy (region): Burgundy's southern shoulder, outside the Côte d'Or.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): Grown here for drinking rather than for keeping.
sources: s:wp-c-te-chalonnaise — Côte Chalonnaise; s:wp-burgundy-wine — Burgundy wine

## Côte de Beaune (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/cote-de-beaune/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/cote-de-beaune.json
id: cote-de-beaune
facets: country=France · level=district
region: Côte de Beaune, Burgundy
what: From Ladoix south to Maranges, where the hill turns and chardonnay takes the best of it. Corton is its only red grand cru; the reds that matter most sit in Pommard, Volnay and Beaune at premier cru.
geo: 46.98, 4.78 (region)
- kin → burgundy (region): The southern half of the Côte d'Or.
- kin → corton (vineyard): The hill that holds the district's only red grand cru.
- kin → chardonnay (variety): The grape that takes the white flank of the same slope.
- kin → hospices-de-beaune (org): Whose vines sit mostly in these communes.
sources: s:wp-c-te-de-beaune — Côte de Beaune; s:wp-burgundy-wine — Burgundy wine
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Côte de Nuits (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/cote-de-nuits/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/cote-de-nuits.json
id: cote-de-nuits
facets: country=France · level=district · soil=limestone, marl, scree
region: Côte de Nuits, Burgundy
what: Fourteen communes between Dijon and Corgoloin holding 24 of Burgundy's 25 red grand cru appellations. Some of them are tiny — La Romanée covers less than a hectare.
how: The good ground sits mid-slope, where the scree drains and the sun reaches. Flat land near the village makes village wine; the top of the hill goes cold and thin.
geo: 47.17, 4.95 (region)
- kin → burgundy (region): The northern half of the Côte d'Or.
- kin → romanee-conti (vineyard): The 1.8-hectare monopole at the centre of the argument.
- kin → clos-de-vougeot (vineyard): Fifty hectares, eighty owners, one grand cru name.
- kin → chambertin (vineyard): Gevrey's grand cru, and the one Napoleon is said to have carried.
- kin → musigny (vineyard): Chambolle's grand cru, where the wine goes lace-fine.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/cote-de-nuits/cote-de-nuits-weinberg-cote-de-nuits.jpg · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Stefan Bauer, https://www.ferras.at · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AWeinberg_Cote_de_Nuits.jpg
sources: s:wp-c-te-de-nuits — Côte de Nuits; s:wp-burgundy-wine — Burgundy wine
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Dundee Hills (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/dundee-hills/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/dundee-hills.json
id: dundee-hills
facets: country=United States · level=sub-ava · established=2004 · soil=Jory — basalt-derived red clay loam

## Santa Maria Valley (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/santa-maria-valley/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/santa-maria-valley.json
id: santa-maria-valley
facets: country=United States · level=ava · established=1981 · soil=sandy loam to clay loam; alluvial floor, shaly slopes
region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County, Central Coast, California
what: A funnel opening west to the Pacific at 34.9°N — further south than anywhere sensible for pinot noir, and colder through the growing season than most of Oregon. The transverse ranges turn this valley east-west, the ocean walks straight in, and summer averages 75°F.
story: Grapes grew here in the 1830s, under the Mexican land grants. Modern planting starts in 1964 with a hundred acres; by the mid-1970s there were over 2,000. The AVA came on 5 August 1981 — the country's third, California's second, and the first for either county. In 2010 the TTB pushed the southern line out to the watershed, adding 18,790 acres and nine vineyards.
how: Morning fog takes hours to burn off and afternoon wind replaces it. Winkler Region I. Under 14 inches of rain in a normal year, so nearly everything is irrigated.
today: Pinot noir and chardonnay are the appellation's two flagship varieties — and the same valley cooks the beef that made it famous, over oak cut off these hills.
geo: 34.93, -120.25 (region)
- kin → bien-nacido (vineyard): The bench planting that sells this valley's fruit to half of California.
- kin → tri-tip-over-red-oak (story): Beef, red oak and pinot noir out of one valley — the long version.
- kin → santa-maria-tri-tip (pairing): What the valley eats, and the argument about what to pour with it.
- kin → sta-rita-hills (region): The county's other pinot valley, half an hour south.
- kin → au-bon-climat (producer): Jim Clendenen's winery, built inside Bien Nacido.
- kin → santa-maria-bbq-association (org): The body that polices what the phrase on the menu means.
sources: s:wp-santa-maria-valley-ava — Santa Maria Valley AVA; s:ecfr-27-9 — 27 CFR part 9 — American Viticultural Areas; s:wp-santa-maria-valley — Santa Maria Valley AVA
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

aliases: Santa Rita Hills
facets: country=United States · level=sub-ava · established=2001 · soil=diatomaceous shale, sandy loam
region: Sta. Rita Hills, Santa Barbara County, California
what: A wind tunnel between Buellton and Lompoc where the Santa Ynez Valley opens west to the ocean. Fog in the morning, thirty-knot afternoons, and some of the slowest ripening in California.
story: Petitioned by growers inside the Santa Ynez Valley AVA who wanted their own name, and established as Santa Rita Hills in 2001. Chile's Viña Santa Rita objected; the TTB shortened it to Sta. Rita Hills in 2005, and the label now carries an abbreviation nobody says out loud.

## Willamette Valley (region)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/region/willamette-valley/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/region/willamette-valley.json
id: willamette-valley
facets: country=United States · level=ava · established=1983 · soil=volcanic Jory, marine sedimentary, windblown loess
region: Willamette Valley, Oregon
what: Three and a half million acres of Oregon between the Coast Range and the Cascades, of which a thin band of hillside grows pinot noir. Eleven AVAs now sit inside it.
story: David Lett planted pinot noir at Dundee in 1965 against the advice of everyone at Davis, who said Oregon was too cold and too wet. His 1975 Eyrie South Block Reserve placed tenth in a 1979 Paris tasting, Robert Drouhin re-ran the comparison in Beaune the following year, and the Burgundians started buying land. Adelsheim chaired the committee that petitioned for the AVA in 1983.
how: Cool and wet, with rain that arrives near harvest and decides the vintage. Growers pick on the forecast as much as on sugar.
today: Pinot noir covered 24,729 acres of Oregon in 2022 and brought the highest price per ton of any variety in the state.
geo: 45.2, -123.1 (region)
- kin → dundee-hills (region): The red Jory hills where Oregon pinot started.
- kin → eola-amity-hills (region): The gap that lets the Van Duzer wind through.
- kin → yamhill-carlton (region): Old marine sediment, and vines that ripen early.
- kin → ribbon-ridge (region): A single small ridge, its own AVA.
- kin → david-lett (person): Who planted the first pinot noir here and argued for the rest.
- kin → eyrie-vineyards (producer): The winery that made the 1975 that changed the argument.
- kin → domaine-drouhin-oregon (producer): Burgundy buying in, four years after the tasting.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/willamette-valley/willamette-valley-vineyard-in-willamette-valley.jpg · CC BY-SA 2.0 · David Burn · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AVineyard_in_Willamette_Valley.jpg
sources: s:wp-willamette-valley-ava — Willamette Valley AVA; s:wp-oregon-wine — Oregon wine; s:ecfr-27-9 — 27 CFR part 9 — American Viticultural Areas
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Bien Nacido (vineyard)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/vineyard/bien-nacido/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/vineyard/bien-nacido.json
id: bien-nacido
aliases: Bien Nacido Vineyards · Rancho Tepusquet
facets: country=United States · established=1969 · soil=sand, chalk and marine loam
region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County, California
what: Eight hundred acres on the Santa Maria bench, planted in 1969 and farmed row by row for whoever buys the rows. Over 250 acres of it is pinot noir, and the vineyard's name appears on more labels than most wineries manage.
story: Tomás Olivera took the Rancho Tepusquet grant from Governor Alvarado in 1837; Chumash had fished Tepusquet Creek long before that. Juan Pacífico Ontiveros built the adobe in 1857 and farmed grain, stock and wine grapes. The Millers bought in 1969, reunited two parcels of the grant and planted vines.
how: Blocks are sold by area rather than by the ton, so a winemaker who wants to crop hard is not arguing with a grower paid by weight. Some customers have bought the same rows for over twenty years and print the block on the label.
today: Also one of California's larger sources of certified budwood — a good deal of the state's chardonnay started as cuttings from here.
geo: 34.92, -120.25 (street)
- kin → santa-maria-valley (region): The AVA it helped define.
- kin → au-bon-climat (producer): Jim Clendenen's winery, on the property.
- kin → tri-tip-over-red-oak (story): The same ranch land that fed the vaquero barbecues.
- kin → massale-selection (practice): What a budwood block is for.

## Clos de Vougeot (vineyard)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/vineyard/clos-de-vougeot/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/vineyard/clos-de-vougeot.json
id: clos-de-vougeot
facets: country=France · soil=limestone at the top, clay at the bottom
region: Côte de Nuits, Burgundy
what: Fifty hectares behind a wall the Cistercians of Cîteaux built, and more than eighty owners inside it. One name on every label, and a slope that runs from grand cru ground at the top to heavy clay by the road.
story: Bought or gifted to the monks between the twelfth and early fourteenth centuries, farmed as one block for six hundred years, then broken up after the Revolution and split again at every inheritance. The wall is the appellation; the ground inside it is not one thing.
geo: 47.176, 4.955 (street)
- kin → cote-de-nuits (region): The district it sits in.
- kin → climat (term): The unit this vineyard is usually held up to explain — and to complicate.
- kin → burgundy (region): Where dividing land by inheritance became the system.

## Romanée-Conti (vineyard)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/vineyard/romanee-conti/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/vineyard/romanee-conti.json
id: romanee-conti
facets: country=France · established=1936 · soil=limestone, marl · status=open
region: Côte de Nuits, Burgundy
what: Under two hectares of Vosne-Romanée hillside, held by one owner, producing about 3,500 bottles a year. No other patch of ground in wine carries this much argument per square metre.
story: Louis François de Bourbon, prince de Conti, bought it in 1760 through an agent and kept the wine for himself; the name stuck. It survived phylloxera on ungrafted vines until 1945, when the harvest fell to about 2.5 hl/ha and 600 bottles, and the vineyard was pulled and replanted.
geo: 47.163, 4.955 (street)
- kin → drc (producer): Its sole owner, and the domaine named after it.
- kin → la-tache (vineyard): The other monopole down the same slope.
- kin → cote-de-nuits (region): The district it sits in.
- kin → monopole (term): One owner, one vineyard — the word for this arrangement.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/romanee-conti/romanee-conti-roman-e-conti-vineyard.jpg · CC BY 2.0 · Andrea Schaffer · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ARoman%C3%A9e-Conti_vineyard.jpg

## Sanford & Benedict (vineyard)

id: sanford-and-benedict
facets: country=United States · established=1971
region: Sta. Rita Hills, Santa Barbara County, California
what: The planting that proved the Santa Ynez river gap: put in during 1971 by Richard Sanford and Michael Benedict on a north-facing slope nobody else wanted, and now inside the Sta. Rita Hills AVA.
story: *Tradition holds —* Sanford went looking with weather records rather than with a realtor, hunting a valley that ran east-west so the ocean air could reach the vines. The old block still gets picked separately and named on labels made by people who never owned it.
geo: 34.62, -120.3 (street)

## Calera (producer)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/producer/calera/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/producer/calera.json
id: calera
facets: country=United States · established=1975
region: California
what: Josh Jensen went looking for limestone in California because Burgundy grows on it, found a lime kiln site high on Mount Harlan in San Benito County, and planted pinot noir at 2,200 feet in 1975.
story: Jensen worked harvests at the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and at Dujac, came home with an idea about soil, and spent a year with geological survey maps before buying. Marq de Villiers wrote a book about the place in 1993.
address: Hollister, CA

## Domaine de la Romanée-Conti (producer)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/producer/drc/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/producer/drc.json
id: drc
aliases: DRC · Domaine de la Romanee-Conti
facets: country=France · status=unknown
region: Côte de Nuits, Burgundy
what: The Vosne-Romanée domaine that owns Romanée-Conti and La Tâche outright and holds pieces of Richebourg, Échezeaux, Grands Échezeaux, Romanée-Saint-Vivant and Montrachet. Sold in mixed cases, allocated by relationship, and resold at multiples nobody at the domaine sets.
story: The Abbey of Saint-Vivant in Vosne held 1.8 hectares here from 1232. The prince de Conti bought the parcel in 1760; the Revolution sold it on; the Villaine and Leroy families have run the domaine through the twentieth century. Five hectares in La Tâche and Grands Échezeaux went biodynamic first, and the practice spread from there.
address: Vosne-Romanée, Côte-d'Or
geo: 47.162, 4.951 (street)
- kin → romanee-conti (vineyard): Its monopole, and its name.
- kin → la-tache (vineyard): Its other monopole.
- kin → aubert-de-villaine (person): Co-director, and the man who carried the Climats to UNESCO.
- kin → burgundy (region): The region whose reputation this address both makes and distorts.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/drc/drc-domaine-de-la-roman-e-conti-7309836076.jpg · CC BY 2.0 · Michal Osmenda from Brussels, Belgium · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ADomaine_de_la_Roman%C3%A9e-Conti_%287309836076%29.jpg

## The Eyrie Vineyards (producer)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/producer/eyrie-vineyards/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/producer/eyrie-vineyards.json
id: eyrie-vineyards
facets: country=United States · established=1965
region: Willamette Valley, Oregon
what: David and Diana Lett planted the Willamette Valley's first pinot noir in 1965 and made their first vintage in 1970. They also made the first American pinot gris.
story: Lett went to Oregon against the advice of his professors at Davis, who held that the state was too cold and too wet for vinifera. The 1975 South Block Reserve placed tenth in a Paris tasting in 1979 and second, by fractions, in Robert Drouhin's rematch in Beaune the year after.
address: McMinnville, OR
geo: 45.21, -123.2 (street)
- kin → david-lett (person): Who planted it.
- kin → dundee-hills (region): The hill his first block sits on.
- kin → willamette-valley (region): The valley he argued into existence as a wine region.
- kin → how-pinot-travelled (story): One leg of the journey, told at length.

id: abel-clone
aliases: Ata Rangi clone · gumboot clone
facets: origin=Burgundy field selection
region: New Zealand, Martinborough, Central Otago
what: New Zealand's most-told vine story: a cutting confiscated at Auckland airport in the 1970s, handed to a customs officer who happened to make wine, propagated, and now planted the length of the country.
story: *Tradition holds —* the cutting came from the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, in a traveller's boot, and Malcolm Abel took it home. The nickname 'gumboot' is the version of the story New Zealand prefers to tell. Its origin has never been documented publicly; its behaviour in the vineyard has.
- kin → martinborough (region): Where it was first propagated in quantity.
- kin → central-otago (region): And where it now grows, 900 km further south.
- kin → massale-selection (practice): The practice this story sits at the edge of.
sources: s:wp-new-zealand-wine — New Zealand wine
provenance default: tradition · confidence: low · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-16

## Calera selection (clone)

aliases: Jensen selection
facets: origin=California
region: California
what: Cuttings Josh Jensen is said to have brought back from Burgundy in the mid-1970s, planted on Mount Harlan and passed around California since. Growers who plant it say so on the label.

- kin → calera (producer): The vineyard it is named for.
- kin → josh-jensen (person): Who carried it, by the usual account.
- kin → massale-selection (practice): The practice, and its grey areas.

## Mount Eden selection (clone)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/clone/mount-eden/

id: mount-eden
aliases: Mt. Eden clone · Martin Ray selection
facets: origin=California
region: Santa Cruz Mountains, California
what: A California field selection traced back to Martin Ray's plantings in the Santa Cruz Mountains, and through him, by the usual account, to Paul Masson's cuttings from Burgundy. Tiny clusters, tiny crop.
story: *Tradition holds —* Masson brought vines from Burgundy to the Santa Cruz Mountains in the 1890s and Ray carried the line forward. The chain is repeated in the trade far more often than it is documented.
- kin → martin-ray (person): Whose vineyard the cuttings came from.

- kin → massale-selection (practice): How a selection like this moves: cuttings, not catalogues.

## Pinot Droit (clone)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/clone/pinot-droit/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/clone/pinot-droit.json
id: pinot-droit
aliases: Gamay Beaujolais (Californian misnomer)
facets: origin=Burgundy field selection
region: California, Burgundy
what: Upright-growing, high-cropping selections that suited a grower paid by weight. California sold a series of them under the misnomer 'Gamay Beaujolais', and Burgundy planted them in ground where nobody was looking.
how: Productive in warm flowering conditions and broad-shouldered in the glass. Growers who wanted a lighter, decumbent vine call those 'pinot fin' or 'pinot tordu' instead.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The same variety, selected for a different habit.
- kin → the-dijon-numbers (story): What replaced it, and why growers changed their minds.

## Pommard, UCD 4 (clone)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/clone/pommard-ucd4/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/clone/pommard-ucd4.json
id: pommard-ucd4
aliases: UCD 4 · Pommard clone · UCD4
facets: origin=Burgundy field selection · country=United States
region: Oregon, California
what: The workhorse of American pinot noir before the Dijon numbers arrived, and still planted everywhere. Bigger berries, firmer structure, a darker wine than the Dijons give.
how: Held and distributed through UC Davis, which is where the number comes from. Oregon built its early reputation on this and on Wädenswil.
- kin → wadenswil-ucd2a (clone): The other half of Oregon's old plantings.
- kin → dijon-115 (clone): What arrived later and changed the arithmetic.
- kin → the-dijon-numbers (story): Why a vine has a catalogue number at all.

## Cold soak (practice)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/practice/cold-soak/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/practice/cold-soak.json
id: cold-soak
aliases: Pre-fermentation maceration · Macération à froid
facets: kind=ferment
region: The world
what: Chilling the crushed fruit and holding it below fermentation temperature for days before the yeast start. Water pulls colour and aroma out of the skins; alcohol has not arrived yet to pull tannin.
how: Three to six days near 10 °C, usually under dry ice or a blanket of CO₂ to keep spoilage organisms and oxygen out. Whether it does what its advocates claim is one of the livelier arguments in a pinot cellar.
- kin → whole-cluster (practice): A decision taken at the same moment, on the same fruit.
- kin → native-yeast (practice): Cold soak lasts until something starts the ferment — which is where this comes in.
sources: s:wp-maceration-wine — Maceration (wine)
provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Green harvest (practice)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/practice/green-harvest/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/practice/green-harvest.json
id: green-harvest
aliases: Vendange verte · Crop thinning
facets: kind=vineyard
region: The world
what: Cutting unripe bunches onto the ground in summer so the vine ripens fewer. Yield control with secateurs, after the vine has already set more fruit than the grower wants.
how: Pinot crops generously if allowed to; appellation rules cap yield, and growers who want concentration cut below the cap. Done too late, the remaining berries just get bigger.
- kin → burgundy (region): Where the yield caps are written into the appellation.
- kin → high-density-planting (practice): The other way to make each vine carry less.
sources: s:oxford-companion-wine-4 — The Oxford Companion to Wine
provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Hand harvest (practice)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/practice/hand-harvest/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/practice/hand-harvest.json
id: hand-harvest
facets: kind=vineyard
region: The world
what: Picking into small crates by hand, so the bunch arrives whole and the cellar decides what to do with it. A machine strips berries off the stem in the row, which settles the whole-cluster question before anyone gets a vote.
how: Whole-cluster work, sorting tables and cold soaks all assume intact fruit. Steep slopes settle it anyway: no machine drives the Côte d'Or's mid-slope.
- kin → whole-cluster (practice): The decision hand-picking keeps open.
- kin → burgundy (region): Where the slope makes the choice for you.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/hand-harvest/hand-harvest-hand-harvesting-in-the-vaucluse.jpg · CC BY 2.0 · Steven Verbruggen · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AHand_harvesting_in_the_Vaucluse.jpg
sources: s:oxford-companion-wine-4 — The Oxford Companion to Wine
provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## High-density planting (practice)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/practice/high-density-planting/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/practice/high-density-planting.json
id: high-density-planting
facets: kind=planting
region: Burgundy, The world
what: Nine to twelve thousand vines a hectare, rows a metre apart, each vine carrying a handful of bunches. Burgundy's grand cru rules set a floor of 9,000 vines per hectare and the New World mostly did not follow.
how: More vines, more competition, smaller root systems each, less fruit per plant at the same yield per hectare. It also means narrow tractors, more labour and more money in the ground before the first harvest.
- kin → la-tache (vineyard): Where the 9,000-vine minimum is written into the appellation.
- kin → bass-phillip (producer): Which planted at Burgundian density in Gippsland and waited twelve years to sell a bottle.
sources: s:wp-la-t-che-aoc — La Tâche AOC; s:wp-bass-phillip — Bass Phillip
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Malolactic fermentation (practice)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/practice/malolactic/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/practice/malolactic.json
id: malolactic
aliases: Malo · MLF · Secondary fermentation
facets: kind=ferment
region: The world
what: A bacterial conversion, not a yeast one: lactic acid bacteria turn sharp malic acid into softer lactic acid and let off CO₂. Nearly every red pinot noir goes through it.
how: Usually after the alcoholic ferment, often in barrel over the winter, and in cold cellars it can wait until spring warms the room. It lowers total acidity, raises pH and can leave a buttery note from diacetyl.
- kin → neutral-oak (practice): Where it usually happens: in barrel, over a cold winter.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): A high-acid grape, which is why the softening matters here.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/malolactic/malolactic-cave-de-bourgogne.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Arnaud 25 · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ACave_de_Bourgogne.jpg
sources: s:wp-malolactic-fermentation — Malolactic fermentation
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Massal selection (practice)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/practice/massale-selection/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/practice/massale-selection.json
id: massale-selection
aliases: Sélection massale · Massale
facets: kind=planting
region: Burgundy, The world
what: Taking cuttings from many vines in a block you already trust, instead of ordering one numbered clone from a nursery. You keep the block's variation, and whatever virus it carries.
how: A grower walks the old block at harvest, marks the vines that ripen well and crop lightly, and grafts from them. The pay-off is diversity inside one vineyard; the risk is leafroll and fanleaf, which is precisely what clonal certification was invented to stop.
- kin → the-dijon-numbers (story): The alternative, and how it won the nursery trade.
- kin → mount-eden (clone): A selection that travelled this way.
- kin → abel-clone (clone): And one whose travel was less orthodox.
- kin → bien-nacido (vineyard): Where certified budwood gets grown at scale instead.
sources: s:wp-pinot-noir — Pinot noir; s:wp-ampelography — Ampelography
provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Native yeast (practice)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/practice/native-yeast/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/practice/native-yeast.json
id: native-yeast
aliases: Wild ferment · Spontaneous fermentation · Indigenous yeast
facets: kind=ferment
region: The world
what: Letting whatever came in on the fruit and lives in the cellar start the ferment, instead of pitching a selected strain from a packet.
how: The early work is done by non-Saccharomyces species that die off as alcohol rises; Saccharomyces cerevisiae finishes. The risk is a stuck ferment or a population you did not want; the argument for it is the character those first days leave behind.
- kin → cold-soak (practice): What ends a cold soak, if nobody intervenes.
- kin → wine-fault-brett (term): The organism that gets blamed when this goes wrong.
sources: s:wp-yeast-in-winemaking — Yeast in winemaking
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Neutral oak (practice)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/practice/neutral-oak/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/practice/neutral-oak.json
id: neutral-oak
aliases: Old barrels · Used barriques
facets: kind=ageing
region: Burgundy, The world
what: A barrel that has already given up its flavour — third use, fourth, older. It still lets oxygen through the staves and still shapes texture; it just stops tasting of the forest.
how: New oak gives vanillin, toast and tannin, and pinot noir has little weight to hide any of it. Cellars set a percentage of new wood per wine and often drop it for the lighter vineyards.
- kin → malolactic (practice): What happens inside these barrels, over winter.
- kin → hanzell (producer): Which imported French barrels to California and started the argument there.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/neutral-oak/neutral-oak-wine-cave-in-burgundy.jpg · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Philip Larson · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AWine_cave_in_Burgundy.jpg
sources: s:wp-oak-wine — Oak (wine); s:wp-barrel — Barrel
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Punching down (practice)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/practice/pigeage/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/practice/pigeage.json
id: pigeage
aliases: Pigeage · Punch-down
facets: kind=ferment
region: Burgundy, The world
what: Pushing the floating cap of skins back under the wine, by foot or by plunger, several times a day. Pinot's cap rises fast and dries out if nobody moves it.
how: Punching down extracts more gently than pumping over; it also warms the ferment and pushes oxygen in. Count and timing are how a cellar sets tannin without over-extracting a grape that has little to spare.
- kin → whole-cluster (practice): What a foot meets when the stems stay in.
- kin → saignee (practice): The other lever for concentration, pulled before fermentation.
- kin → pigeage-term (term): The word itself.
sources: s:wp-maceration-wine — Maceration (wine); s:wp-fermentation-in-winemaking — Fermentation in winemaking
provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Saignée (practice)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/practice/saignee/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/practice/saignee.json
id: saignee
facets: kind=press
region: The world, Champagne
what: Bleeding juice off a red fermenter early, to raise the skin-to-juice ratio in what stays behind. The juice that comes out is sold as rosé.
how: Runs the other way round from making rosé on purpose: here the pink wine is a by-product of concentrating the red, and it tastes like one unless the fruit was picked with it in mind.
- kin → saignee-term (term): The word, from saigner, to bleed.
- kin → champagne (region): Where rosé is more often made by blending red wine in instead.
sources: s:wp-ros — Rosé; s:oxford-companion-wine-4 — The Oxford Companion to Wine
provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Whole cluster (practice)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/practice/whole-cluster/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/practice/whole-cluster.json
id: whole-cluster
aliases: Whole-bunch · Vendange entière · Stem inclusion
facets: kind=ferment
region: Burgundy, The world
what: Putting bunches into the fermenter with their stems still attached, instead of pulling the berries off first. Stems bring water, potassium, tannin and a green-stalk smell that turns spicy when it works and stalky when it doesn't.
how: Stems raise pH by absorbing acid, cool the ferment by taking up heat, and build a lattice that lets a cap breathe. Growers pick a percentage — 30%, 50%, all of it — and argue about it forever. Ripe lignified stems help; green ones taste like the pruning pile.
- kin → vendange-entiere (term): The French word, and its root.
- kin → pigeage (practice): The other half of the same fermentation decision.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): A variety thin enough in tannin to notice what the stems add.
sources: s:wp-maceration-wine — Maceration (wine); s:oxford-companion-wine-4 — The Oxford Companion to Wine
provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Coq au vin (pairing)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/pairing/coq-au-vin/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/pairing/coq-au-vin.json
id: coq-au-vin
facets: course=main · country=France
region: Burgundy
what: A tough old bird braised in red wine, lardons, mushrooms and onions, thickened with its own blood in the oldest versions. Burgundy cooks it in Burgundy and drinks the same wine with it.
story: The dish attaches itself to Julius Caesar in the usual apocryphal way. What it is, plainly, is a way to make a rooster edible: long, slow, wet heat and acid.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The wine in the pot and in the glass.
- kin → burgundy (region): Where the version with a named wine comes from.
- kin → mushrooms (pairing): In the pot from the start.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/coq-au-vin/coq-au-vin-coq-au-vin.jpg · CC BY 2.5 · MattHucke at en.wikipedia · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ACoq_au_vin.jpg
sources: s:wp-coq-au-vin — Coq au vin
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Duck (pairing)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/pairing/duck/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/pairing/duck.json
id: duck
facets: course=bird · country=France
region: Burgundy, The world
what: The pairing pinot noir gets asked about most: dark meat, a thick fat cap, and enough savoury weight to meet a wine with little tannin.
how: Roasted whole, seared as breast, or salted and cooked in its own fat as confit. Fat carries flavour and coats the tongue; a high-acid red cuts through it in a way a low-acid one does not.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The wine most often poured with it.
- kin → burgundy (region): Where the pairing is a house rule.
- kin → mushrooms (pairing): The other half of most plates it arrives on.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/duck/duck-duck-dish-walluf.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Gerda Arendt · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ADuck_dish%2C_Walluf.jpg
sources: s:wp-duck-as-food — Duck as food; s:wp-wine-and-food-matching — Wine and food pairing
provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Mushrooms (pairing)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/pairing/mushrooms/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/pairing/mushrooms.json
id: mushrooms
facets: course=fungus · country=France
region: Burgundy, Oregon, The world
what: The flavour bridge: older pinot noir picks up a forest-floor smell, and a plate of fungi meets it head on. Glutamates in the mushroom read as savoury, which is the same register a mature bottle moves into.
- kin → duck (pairing): Its usual companion on the plate.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The wine whose aged character it mirrors.
- kin → truffle-pairing (pairing): The expensive end of the same idea.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/mushrooms/mushrooms-edible-fungi-in-basket-2009-g1.jpg · Public domain · George Chernilevsky · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AEdible_fungi_in_basket_2009_G1.jpg

provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Pinquito beans (pairing)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/pairing/pinquito-beans/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/pairing/pinquito-beans.json
id: pinquito-beans
aliases: Pinquitos
facets: course=side · country=United States
region: Santa Maria Valley, California
what: A small pink bean grown in the Santa Maria Valley and almost nowhere else, cooked with bacon or ham, garlic, chilli and a little tomato, and served in a bowl beside the beef.
story: Considered indigenous to this valley; a cross between a pink bean and a small white one. Betteravia Farms began growing them commercially in 1972, and a handful of local brands still supply the barbecue trade.
- kin → santa-maria-tri-tip (pairing): The plate it belongs to.
- kin → santa-maria-valley (region): The only ground that grows them at scale.
sources: s:wp-santa-maria-style-barbecue — Santa Maria–style barbecue
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Red oak (pairing)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/pairing/red-oak/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/pairing/red-oak.json
id: red-oak
aliases: Coast live oak · Quercus agrifolia · Encina
facets: course=condiment · country=United States
region: Santa Maria Valley, California
what: The wood the whole style rests on. In Santa Maria, red oak means coast live oak — Quercus agrifolia — which grows on the hills around the valley and burns down to hot, steady coals without throwing much smoke.
how: Split, burned down to coals in a firebox or at the edge of the pit, then raked under a grate on a hand crank. The cook moves the meat up and down instead of moving the fire. Little smoke matters here: the valley is windy, and the cooking is hot and quick rather than long and low.
notes: The local name turns out to be good botany. Coast live oak is a semi-evergreen oak of the California Floristic Province, growing from Mendocino south into northern Baja, and it sits in the red oak section of the genus — though unusually for that group its acorns ripen in seven or eight months rather than eighteen. Californio Spanish called the tree encina, which is why Encinitas and Encinal are on the map.
- kin → santa-maria-tri-tip (pairing): The meat it cooks.
- kin → tri-tip-over-red-oak (story): Why the wood is the part that cannot be exported.
- kin → santa-maria-valley (region): The hills it grows on.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/red-oak/red-oak-quercus-agrifolia-6.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Eugene Zelenko · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AQuercus_agrifolia-6.jpg
sources: s:wp-quercus-agrifolia — Quercus agrifolia; s:wp-santa-maria-style-barbecue — Santa Maria–style barbecue
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Salmon (pairing)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/pairing/salmon/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/pairing/salmon.json
id: salmon
facets: course=fish · country=United States
region: Oregon, Willamette Valley
what: A fish oily enough to take a red wine, and in Oregon the pairing is local logic rather than theory — the fish and the pinot come from the same watershed.
how: Grilled over alder, or roasted. The oil in the flesh and the char off the fire both find something to do with a light red.
- kin → ipnc (event): Where a valley full of growers eats it every summer.
- kin → willamette-valley (region): The valley that grows the wine beside the river.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The red that gets poured with fish without an argument.

## Santa Maria salsa (pairing)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/pairing/santa-maria-salsa/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/pairing/santa-maria-salsa.json
id: santa-maria-salsa
facets: course=condiment · country=United States
region: Santa Maria Valley, California
what: Chopped raw tomato, celery, green chilli, onion and a shot of vinegar or Worcestershire — thinner and sharper than a Mexican pico de gallo, and spooned over sliced beef rather than eaten with chips.
how: The acid is the point: the meat is lean and salty, and the salsa cuts it. That also changes what happens when you drink something with it.
- kin → santa-maria-tri-tip (pairing): What it goes on.
- kin → tri-tip-over-red-oak (story): Where the acid question meets the wine question.
sources: s:wp-santa-maria-style-barbecue — Santa Maria–style barbecue; s:wp-salsa-sauce — Salsa (food)

## Santa Maria tri-tip (pairing)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/pairing/santa-maria-tri-tip/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/pairing/santa-maria-tri-tip.json
id: santa-maria-tri-tip
aliases: Tri-tip · Santa Maria steak · Triangle tip · Newport steak
facets: course=main · country=United States
region: Santa Maria Valley, California
what: A triangular two-to-five-pound piece of bottom sirloin, rolled in salt, pepper and garlic, grilled over red oak coals to medium-rare and sliced across the grain. In its home valley it arrives with pinquito beans, salsa, green salad and buttered French bread grilled on the same fire.
story: The barbecue is older than the cut. Californio ranchers fed their vaqueros each spring from oak-coal pits, and the Santa Maria Club ran a stag barbecue for up to 700 people a month from 1931. Top sirloin was the meat. In the late 1950s a market manager in Santa Maria put a triangular piece that usually went to the grinder on a rotisserie instead, and by the 1960s the town had a cut of its own.
how: Grill directly over red oak, fat side up, turning once; pull at 130–135 °F and let it rest before slicing. The grain changes direction inside the muscle, so the knife has to change with it. Central California butchers leave the fat cap on; butchers elsewhere trim it.
today: Sold country-wide now, and still the default thing to cook at a Santa Maria Valley fundraiser, rodeo or school benefit.
geo: 34.953, -120.436 (town)
- kin → tri-tip-over-red-oak (story): The long version: the ranch, the oak, the competing claims, and the wine question.
- kin → red-oak (pairing): The wood, which is not a red oak.
- kin → pinquito-beans (pairing): What comes beside it.
- kin → santa-maria-salsa (pairing): And what goes on it.
- kin → santa-maria-valley (region): The valley that also grows pinot noir on the same hills.
- kin → bob-schutz (person): The market manager the town credits.
- kin → santa-maria-bbq-association (org): Which defines the phrase on the menu.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/images/santa-maria-tri-tip/santa-maria-tri-tip-santamaria-stylebbq.jpg · CC BY 2.0 · Eugene Kim from San Francisco, USA · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ASantaMaria-StyleBBQ.jpg
sources: s:wp-santa-maria-style-barbecue — Santa Maria–style barbecue; s:wp-tri-tip — Tri-tip; s:usda-imps-100 — Institutional Meat Purchase Specifications, Series 100 — Fresh Beef; s:web-smv-bbq-association — Santa Maria Style Barbeque Association; s:wp-cut-of-beef — Cut of beef
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

id: washed-rind-cheese
facets: course=cheese · country=France
region: Burgundy
what: Époisses, Soumaintrain, Langres — Burgundy's own cheeses, washed in brine and marc until they smell like a farmyard and taste milder than they smell. The classic local match, and a difficult one: the same wash that makes the rind pungent can flatten a delicate bottle.

## Bob Schutz (person)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/person/bob-schutz/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/person/bob-schutz.json
id: bob-schutz
facets: role=butcher · country=United States
region: Santa Maria Valley, California
what: A Santa Maria market manager who, in the late 1950s, took a triangular piece of bottom sirloin that was going into the hamburger grinder, seasoned it and put it on a rotisserie. The cut he sold as tri-tip is now the whole town's dish.
story: The account comes from Larry Viegas, a butcher who worked with him at a Santa Maria Safeway: an excess of hamburger meat, a piece nobody wanted, salt, pepper and garlic salt, forty-five minutes to an hour on the spit. Other people claim the cut elsewhere — an Army butcher in southern California during the war, an Oakland butcher, a New York restaurateur — and the tri-tip record lays those out side by side.
- kin → santa-maria-tri-tip (pairing): The dish that followed.
- kin → tri-tip-over-red-oak (story): Every claim to the cut, in order.
- kin → santa-maria-valley (region): His town, and the valley it made famous.
sources: s:wp-tri-tip — Tri-tip; s:wp-santa-maria-style-barbecue — Santa Maria–style barbecue
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## David Lett (person)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/person/david-lett/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/person/david-lett.json
id: david-lett
facets: role=grower · country=United States
region: Willamette Valley, Oregon
what: Left UC Davis in 1964 with a degree and a plan to grow pinot noir outside Burgundy, and in 1965 planted it in the Willamette Valley — against the advice of every professor he had.
story: His 1975 Eyrie South Block Reserve placed tenth in a 1979 Paris tasting of pinot noir. Robert Drouhin ran the comparison again in Beaune in 1980, where it came second by a fraction to one of his own wines, and Burgundy took Oregon seriously from then on.
- kin → eyrie-vineyards (producer): The winery he founded.
- kin → willamette-valley (region): The valley he bet on.
- kin → pinot-gris (variety): And the first American planting of it.

## Henri Jayer (person)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/person/henri-jayer/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/person/henri-jayer.json
id: henri-jayer
facets: role=winemaker · country=France
region: Côte de Nuits, Burgundy
what: A Vosne-Romanée grower who started with a 3-hectare inheritance in the 1950s and changed how the Côte handles pinot noir — destemming, cold soak before fermentation, no filtration, clean fruit above all.
story: He read oenology at Dijon in the 1940s and farmed parcels in Échezeaux and Beaux Monts. His bottles now sell for more than almost any other Burgundy at auction, which is a fact about the market, not about the wine in the bottle.
- kin → richebourg (vineyard): One of the parcels his name is attached to.
- kin → cold-soak (practice): A practice his cellar made standard on the Côte.
- kin → cote-de-nuits (region): Where he worked all his life.

## Jim Clendenen (person)

id: jim-clendenen
facets: role=winemaker · country=United States
region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County, California
what: Founded Au Bon Climat in 1982 and spent forty years making Burgundian varieties on the Central Coast — big hair, big arguments, and a refusal to chase ripeness when everyone else did.
story: Born in Akron in 1953, died in 2021. Santa Barbara County called him the godfather of its wine trade, and he pushed the county's pinot noir and chardonnay into export markets that had not previously looked south of Monterey.

## Hospices de Beaune (org)

## TTB (org)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/org/ttb/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/org/ttb.json
id: ttb
aliases: Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau
facets: country=United States · kind=appellation · status=open
region: California, Oregon
what: The US Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau: it rules on AVA petitions, writes them into 27 CFR part 9, and approves every label that goes on a bottle.
how: An AVA petition has to show the name is already used for the place, propose a boundary, and show the growing conditions differ from the ground around it. Nothing in the rule speaks to quality.
geo: 38.9, -77.03 (town)
- kin → ava (term): The instrument it administers.
- kin → santa-maria-valley (region): Established under its predecessor bureau in 1981.
- kin → sta-rita-hills (region): And renamed by the TTB in 2005 after a trademark objection.

## AVA (term)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/word/ava/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/term/ava.json
id: ava
aliases: American Viticultural Area
root: English initialism; the regulation calls it a 'viticultural area'
facets: letter=A · kind=appellation
region: California, Oregon
what: American Viticultural Area: a boundary drawn around ground with a name, established by federal rule in 27 CFR part 9. It says where the grapes grew and nothing at all about how good they were.
how: Anybody may petition. The petition has to show the name is in use, the boundary is justified and the growing conditions are distinguishable. There is no yield cap, no variety list and no quality tier — which is the whole difference from an AOC.
- kin → santa-maria-valley (region): Established 1981: the country's third.
- kin → ttb (org): The bureau that rules on the petitions.
- kin → burgundy (region): Where the same idea comes with rules about what you may plant and how much you may pick.
sources: s:ecfr-27-9 — 27 CFR part 9 — American Viticultural Areas; s:wp-american-viticultural-area — American Viticultural Area
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Brett (term)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/word/wine-fault-brett/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/term/wine-fault-brett.json
id: wine-fault-brett
aliases: Brettanomyces
root: Latinised Greek: Brettano- (British) + -myces (fungus) — named in a Carlsberg lab from British beer
facets: letter=B · kind=cellar
region: The world
what: Brettanomyces, a yeast that lives in old barrels and makes phenols people describe as barnyard, plaster or clove. Some drinkers read a little of it as complexity, laboratories read it as spoilage, and pinot noir shows it early because there is so little else in the way.
- kin → native-yeast (practice): Whose risk this is.
- kin → neutral-oak (practice): Where it lives, if it lives anywhere.
sources: s:wp-brettanomyces — Brettanomyces; s:wp-wine-fault — Wine fault
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Brix (term)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/word/brix/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/term/brix.json
id: brix
root: Named for Adolf Brix, the nineteenth-century German scientist who refined the scale
facets: letter=B · kind=vineyard
region: California, Oregon
what: Sugar in the juice, as a percentage by weight. Pickers read it off a refractometer in the row, and it is the number most arguments about picking dates are conducted in — usually alongside acid and pH, which matter as much.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): A grape that can hit sugar before its stems and skins are ready.
- kin → hand-harvest (practice): The decision the number feeds into.
sources: s:wp-winemaking — Winemaking
provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Climat (term)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/word/climat/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/term/climat.json
id: climat
root: French climat, from Latin clima, Greek klima — a slope, a zone of the sky; the Burgundian sense is a named plot · the everyday French word for climate is the same word, which confuses every visitor
facets: letter=C · kind=vineyard
region: Burgundy
what: In Burgundy, a named parcel of vineyard with a boundary, a history and a reputation — not a weather word. There are over a thousand of them on the Côte d'Or, and UNESCO listed the lot in 2015.
how: A climat is drawn on the ground, and the appellation rank is attached to it. Two neighbouring climats can differ by a rank and by a factor of ten in price.
- kin → burgundy (region): The region that counts in these units.
- kin → lieu-dit (term): The wider French term a climat is a particular case of.
- kin → clos-de-vougeot (vineyard): One name, fifty hectares, and a lesson about what a climat does not tell you.
sources: s:unesco-1425 — The Climats, terroirs of Burgundy — World Heritage List 1425; s:wp-burgundy-wine — Burgundy wine
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Cru (term)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/word/cru/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/term/cru.json
id: cru
root: French cru, past participle of croître, to grow — 'that which has grown'
facets: letter=C · kind=vineyard
region: Burgundy, The world
what: A growth: a vineyard, or a class of vineyards, recognised for what it yields. Grand cru and premier cru rank the ground in Burgundy; in Bordeaux the same word ranks the château instead.
- kin → climat (term): The plot a cru rank is attached to here.
- kin → burgundy (region): Four ranks, and the smaller the ground the louder the name.
sources: s:wp-grand-cru — Grand cru; s:wp-premier-cru — First Growth
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Négociant (term)

facets: letter=N · kind=cellar

what: A merchant who buys grapes, juice or finished wine, raises it in their own cellar and sells it under their own name. Half of Burgundy's output moves this way.
how: A négociant-éleveur raises what it buys. A domaine bottles only its own fruit. Many houses do both and the label says which is which, if you read the small print.

## The numbers on the vine (story)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/story/the-dijon-numbers/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/story/the-dijon-numbers.json
id: the-dijon-numbers
facets: kind=essay
region: Burgundy, Oregon, The world
what: A grower ordering pinot noir today picks numbers out of a catalogue: 115, 667, 777, or Pommard, or Wädenswil. Each one is a single mother vine, tested clean of virus and copied. That is a twentieth-century invention, and it changed what a vineyard can be.
- kin → dijon-115 (clone): The number planted most.
- kin → massale-selection (practice): The older way, still practised.
- kin → fps (org): Which holds and tests the American material.
- kin → raymond-bernard (person): Who ran the Dijon programme.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): A variety that mutates enough to make all this necessary.

provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Tri-tip over red oak (story)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/story/tri-tip-over-red-oak/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/pinot-noir/api/story/tri-tip-over-red-oak.json
id: tri-tip-over-red-oak
facets: kind=essay · country=United States
region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County, California
what: One California valley cooks beef over local oak, grows pinot noir on the hills that oak comes off, and rarely puts the two together in the same sentence. This page follows both — the ranch barbecue that became a town's dish, the butcher's cut five different people claim, the wood that is the part nobody can ship, and what happens when a thin-skinned grape meets a salted, charred, medium-rare piece of bottom sirloin.
geo: 34.95, -120.3 (region)
- kin → santa-maria-tri-tip (pairing): The dish itself, in one card.
- kin → red-oak (pairing): The wood, and why it stays home.
- kin → pinquito-beans (pairing): The bean that grows nowhere else much.
- kin → santa-maria-salsa (pairing): The acid on the plate.
- kin → santa-maria-valley (region): The AVA on the same ground.
- kin → bien-nacido (vineyard): The vineyard planted on the old Tepusquet grant.
- kin → bob-schutz (person): The man Santa Maria credits with the cut.
- kin → santa-maria-bbq-association (org): Which defines the words on the menu.
- kin → pinot-noir (variety): The grape on the other side of the question.
